title: Bulk rollback & observability handback playbook for cross-surface launches (runtime/console/API)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As we scale coordinated launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces, teams lack an operationally consistent playbook for bulk rollback and for handing back observability ownership after a launch. This increases time-to-recovery, causes duplication of triage work, and leads to unclear SLA impact on customers.

Objective: Create a single playbook and checklist that covers: pre-launch signal contracts, staged rollback lanes (per-region + cross-region), observability handback (dashboards / runbooks ownership), comms and escalation protocol, automated triggers vs manual decision thresholds, and post-rollback validation. The playbook should be consumable by PMs, engineers, and SREs and integrated into the launch calendar so it can be required gating criteria for release trains.

Scope: runtime serving changes (model/quantization/ops), console UX/deploys, public API surface changes. Not in scope: billing system rollbacks (separate runbook).

Deliverables: 
- A machine-friendly checklist template that can be attached to any launch entry in Launch Calendar.
- A decision tree for rollback vs roll-forward with numeric thresholds for latency, error rate, and model-quality regressions.
- Regional fallback plan mapping (which regions to quiesce first, capacity gates).
- Observability handback README: list of dashboards, synthetic checks, trace samples, and ownership toggles.
- Communication templates (Slack, status page, customer comms) and an ops-role matrix for the first 72 hours post-launch.
- A small automation prototype (one GitHub Action + PagerDuty schedule hook) to auto-notify the cross-team launch channel when gate thresholds exceed defined limits.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Playbook reviewed and approved by SRE, Runtime, Console, and API leads.
2) Template can be attached to an existing launch calendar entry and populated in < 20 minutes by launch owners.
3) At least one simulated rollout+rollback exercise completed in staging with runbook and comms, documented with learnings.
4) Automation prototype merged behind feature flag and demoed during the release train dry-run.

Links & artifacts: 
- Draft playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LAUNCH/Bulk+Rollback+Playbook 
- Template checklist (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/launch-templates 
- Draft automation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/914 
- Dry-run plan: https://docs.google.com/document/dry-run-plan
- Slack channel: #launch-runbook (used for coordination and dry-run)

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Teams may skip the checklist under time pressure. Mitigation: Make playbook a gating requirement in the release-train schedule and add a lightweight checkbox on the calendar entry that blocks canary openers.
- Risk: Overly prescriptive thresholds won't fit all model types. Mitigation: Use percent-baseline deltas (e.g., +200% error rate or > 3x p95 latency) with fallback to owner judgment and an 'SRE consult' step.
- Risk: Observability ownership confusion. Mitigation: Strict handback protocol where the owning team tags an oncall and validates dashboard signals before signoff.

Next steps: 
1) Align on thresholds with SRE and Runtime leads (owner: Liam O'Connor) by 2026-03-10.
2) Draft checklist and decision tree and circulate for design review (owner: Ava Martinez) by 2026-03-18.
3) Build automation prototype + PR (owner: infra-eng: Priya Shah) by 2026-03-25.
4) Schedule staging dry-run during release train rehearsal week (owner: launch-ops) week of 2026-03-29.
